headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Ronja is putting together a job application, and everyone has an opinion. Ronja keeps steering the group away from blunt commands and toward softer, more natural German: not "Kannst du?" but "Könntest du?" — the same idea, offered more politely.
objective: See how könnte softens kann into a request, suggestion, or possibility.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: The Abschlussprüfung is close, and everyone has advice for everyone else. Petra keeps steering the group from bare commands toward gentler German: not "Du sollst mehr üben" but "Du solltest mehr üben" — the same idea, offered as advice rather than an order.
objective: See how sollte softens soll into advice, a recommendation, or an opinion.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Rohan just moved into a new flat with a flatmate, a cat, and a view of the mountains — the perfect excuse to swap childhood memories (als) and daily habits (wenn). Frau Weber keeps the test simple: did it happen once, in the past? als. Everything else? wenn.
objective: See the one-question test: one-time past (als) vs. everything else (wenn).

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Week three, and the language school is buzzing: today there\u2019s a small Berufsmesse \u2014 a careers fair \u2014 in the cafeteria. Anna, Rohan and Max wander from table to table meeting a gardener, a bank clerk, a geriatric nurse, and reading brochures about training, work experience and school subjects. Every job, every place, every subject needs its article \u2014 der, die, das \u2014 so it\u2019s the perfect day to make the choice automatic.
scene: Berufsmesse in der Cafeteria \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See the whole article system on one page \u2014 nothing new, all review.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A delayed train, a business trip, and a new hobby give Anna, Rohan, Max and Frau Weber plenty to ask and answer about — without ever repeating the noun. Worauf wartest du? Darauf. Mit wem sprichst du? Mit meiner Kollegin.
objective: See the one idea: wo(r)/da(r) for things, preposition+wem/wen for people.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A café table becomes a crash course in polite German — Anna wants a coffee, Max wants advice about a working day, Rohan needs help, and Frau Weber has a wish for everyone: hätte, wäre, würde, könnte, and sollte, all in one relaxed afternoon.
objective: See the one idea: hätte, wäre, würde make German softer.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A radio show about music and culture gives Anna, Rohan, Max and Frau Weber the perfect excuse to describe people and things in one flowing sentence: der Mann, der …, die Frau, die …, das Lied, das …
objective: See the one idea: der/die/das/die connect two sentences into one.

headline: Everything together — one last time.
intro: The last afternoon before the real exam: Anna, Rohan, Max and Frau Weber compare notes, describe people they admire, wish for a calmer week, and plan the exam morning together. Nothing new — just Chapters 25 through 34, all at once.
scene: Der letzte Nachmittag vor der Prüfung — Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See how Chapters 25–34 fit together — and how the final checkpoint works.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: The morning after the careers fair, the classroom is full of questions \u2014 and every one of them starts with warum? Why medicine, why an apprenticeship, why Germany at all? Frau Weber shows the group the one small move that answers them all: the word weil, and the conjugated verb sliding to the end of the clause. Suddenly everyone can explain themselves.
scene: Der Morgen nach der Berufsmesse \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See the one move: weil sends the verb to the end.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: It\u2019s film-and-media week at the language school. Max has started a small blog about German films, Anna is watching a silent-film classic, and everyone has an opinion \u2014 which is exactly the point. Frau Weber shows them that every "I think\u2026", "I hope\u2026", "I know\u2026" hides the same little engine: the word dass, and the verb sliding to the end, just like weil last week.
objective: See that dass follows the exact weil rule \u2014 verb to the end.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: A quiet Monday, and the class is swapping weekend and childhood stories \u2014 a friend\u2019s wedding, a small emergency with the heating, what everyone was and wasn\u2019t allowed to do as kids. It\u2019s the perfect stage for the modal past: konnte, musste, durfte, wollte, sollte, mochte. Frau Weber shows them that this, not the Perfekt, is how Germans actually say "I had to", "I wanted to", "I was allowed to".
scene: Montagmorgen \u2014 Geschichten vom Wochenende, Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See why modals break the Perfekt habit and use the Pr\u00e4teritum.

headline: Stories that stick.
intro: Pets have taken over the classroom chat: Rohan\u2019s new rabbit, Anna\u2019s neighbour\u2019s barking dog, Max\u2019s childhood cow on a tiny North-Sea island. Every story is about someone and their animal \u2014 which means the dative possessive is everywhere: mit meinem Hund, bei ihren Eltern, das Spielzeug von seinem Hasen. Frau Weber turns the noise into one clean pattern.
scene: Haustiergeschichten vor dem Kursfest \u2014 Sprachschule Berlin
objective: See the three dative endings that every possessive shares.
